encounters.cc: Worsening dysmenorrhea and deep pelvic pain during intercourse with difficulty conceiving for the past year

lines: Worsening dysmenorrhea and deep pelvic pain during intercourse with difficulty conceiving for the past year
The patient is a 30-year-old female with ovarian and bladder endometriosis, polycystic ovary syndrome, and primary infertility who returns for follow-up six months after her initial evaluation.
She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of worsening dysmenorrhea and deep pelvic pain during intercourse.
She also reports difficulty conceiving for the past year despite regular unprotected intercourse.
Her menstrual cycles are regular, with severe cramping beginning one day before menses and lasting through the first two days.
She denies any abnormal vaginal discharge or bleeding.
Her past medical history is significant for a ruptured ovarian cyst at age 24.
- Laparoscopic drainage of ruptured ovarian cyst (age 24)
- Clomiphene citrate 50 mg daily on days 3-7 of menstrual cycle (current ovulation induction protocol)
- Naproxen 500 mg twice daily as needed for dysmenorrhea
- Prenatal vitamin with folic acid 1 tablet daily
- Mother with endometriosis and hysterectomy at age 42
- Maternal cousin with polycystic ovary syndrome
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
On physical examination, the patient exhibits significant discomfort with cervical motion and a fixed, retroverted uterus is palpated.
A lateral displacement of the cervix is noted.
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals several small cystic structures in the ovaries bilaterally.

encounters.cc: 6-month history of worsening pelvic pain, particularly during menstruation, with dyspareunia and menorrhagia

lines: 6-month history of worsening pelvic pain, particularly during menstruation, with dyspareunia and menorrhagia
The patient returns for follow-up of known endometriosis with ovarian and bladder involvement and primary infertility, last evaluated six months ago for worsening dysmenorrhea and deep pelvic pain.
She presents with a 6-month history of worsening pelvic pain, particularly during menstruation.
She reports the pain is sharp and sometimes radiates to her lower back.
She also experiences pain during intercourse.
Her menstrual cycles are regular, but she describes them as very heavy and painful.
She has been trying to conceive for the past year without success.
Her past medical history is significant for a ruptured ovarian cyst 2 years ago.
- Laparoscopic drainage of ruptured ovarian cyst (age 24)
- Clomiphene citrate 50 mg daily on days 3-7 of menstrual cycle (current ovulation induction protocol)
- Naproxen 500 mg twice daily as needed for dysmenorrhea
- Prenatal vitamin with folic acid 1 tablet daily
- Mother with endometriosis and hysterectomy at age 42
- Maternal cousin with polycystic ovary syndrome
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
On physical examination, you note a tender, retroverted uterus and nodularity in the posterior cul-de-sac.
A transvaginal ultrasound reveals several small cysts on both ovaries with no evidence of free fluid or masses.

lines: 6-month history of intermittent hematuria and dysuria with cyclical pattern worsening during menses

She reports that these symptoms seem to occur in a cyclical pattern, worsening during her menstrual periods.
She denies any recent urinary tract infections, and her urine cultures have repeatedly been negative.
Her past medical history is significant for chronic pelvic pain and infertility.
- Laparoscopic drainage of ruptured ovarian cyst (age 24)
- Clomiphene citrate 50 mg daily on days 3-7 of menstrual cycle (current ovulation induction protocol)
- Naproxen 500 mg twice daily as needed for dysmenorrhea

encounters.cc: 3-day history of progressive lower abdominal pain and bloating following ovulation induction

lines: 3-day history of progressive lower abdominal pain and bloating following ovulation induction

This 32-year-old female with endometriosis involving the ovaries and bladder, polycystic ovary syndrome, and primary infertility presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of progressive lower abdominal pain and bloating.
She reports that she has been trying to conceive for the past 2 years and recently underwent ovulation induction with clomiphene.
Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago.
- Laparoscopic drainage of ruptured ovarian cyst (age 24)
- Clomiphene citrate 50 mg daily on days 3-7 of menstrual cycle (current ovulation induction protocol)
- Naproxen 500 mg twice daily as needed for dysmenorrhea
- Prenatal vitamin with folic acid 1 tablet daily
- Mother with endometriosis and hysterectomy at age 42
- Maternal cousin with polycystic ovary syndrome
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
Her vital signs are as follows: blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, heart rate 110 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F).
On examination, her abdomen is distended with shifting dullness.
Pelvic ultrasound shows bilateral enlarged ovaries with multiple cysts.

encounters.cc: Follow-up of primary infertility after 3 months of ovulation induction therapy

lines: Follow-up of primary infertility after 3 months of ovulation induction therapy
The patient with endometriosis and PCOS returns for infertility follow-up after prior hyperstimulation.
She has been receiving pharmacologic ovulation induction for the past 3 months.
Her menstrual cycles were previously irregular, but she has recently achieved consistent ovulation confirmed by mid-luteal progesterone testing.
- Laparoscopic drainage of ruptured ovarian cyst (age 24)
- Clomiphene citrate 50 mg daily on days 3-7 of menstrual cycle (current ovulation induction protocol)
- Naproxen 500 mg twice daily as needed for dysmenorrhea
- Prenatal vitamin with folic acid 1 tablet daily
- Mother with endometriosis and hysterectomy at age 42
- Maternal cousin with polycystic ovary syndrome
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
She feels well today and denies abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, fever, or urinary symptoms.
Laboratory studies are within normal limits
A pelvic ultrasound performed as part of routine monitoring shows bilateral enlarged ovaries with multiple developing follicles.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain with nausea and vomiting

lines: Sudden onset of severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain with nausea and vomiting
This 32-year-old with endometriosis and prior ovarian torsion on ovulation induction presents with severe right lower quadrant pain.
She describes the pain as sharp and constant, and it is associated with nausea and vomiting.
She denies any urinary symptoms, vaginal discharge, or bleeding.
Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago and was normal.
She has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome and has had intermittent mild pelvic pain over the past few months.
- Laparoscopic drainage of ruptured ovarian cyst (age 24)
- Clomiphene citrate 50 mg daily on days 3-7 of menstrual cycle (current ovulation induction protocol)
- Naproxen 500 mg twice daily as needed for dysmenorrhea
- Prenatal vitamin with folic acid 1 tablet daily
- Mother with endometriosis and hysterectomy at age 42
- Maternal cousin with polycystic ovary syndrome
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
On examination, her vital signs are stable,
She appears to be in distress due to pain.
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness and guarding in the right lower quadrant with no rebound tenderness.
Pelvic examination shows a tender adnexal mass on the right side.
A urine pregnancy test is negative.
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals a 5 cm right ovarian cyst with decreased blood flow to the ovary.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of severe right-sided pelvic pain radiating to lower back

lines: Sudden onset of severe right-sided pelvic pain radiating to lower back
The patient with endometriosis involving ovaries and bladder, PCOS, infertility, and prior torsions 2022 on clomiphene presents with recurrent sharp constant pain radiating to her lower back.
She denies vaginal bleeding, discharge, or fever.
Her last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago and was normal.
- Laparoscopic drainage of ruptured ovarian cyst (age 24)
- Clomiphene citrate 50 mg daily on days 3-7 of menstrual cycle (current ovulation induction protocol)
- Naproxen 500 mg twice daily as needed for dysmenorrhea
- Prenatal vitamin with folic acid 1 tablet daily
- Mother with endometriosis and hysterectomy at age 42
- Maternal cousin with polycystic ovary syndrome
- Paternal grandmother with type 2 diabetes mellitus
On physical examination, she appears to be in distress due to pain.
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness in the right lower quadrant with some voluntary guarding.
Pelvic examination is significant for a palpable mass in the right adnexa and pain elicited with cervical motion.
Transvaginal ultrasound shows a 5 cm complex, heterogeneous mass in the right ovary with decreased blood flow to the ovary.
